name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.exists_unit_eigenvector_of_character_ne_infinity
title: A character becomes a joint unit eigenvector

content.display_title: A character becomes a joint unit eigenvector
content.one_sentence_role: Transfers a normalized GNS eigenvector to the given representation through a unitary with a specified direction.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed and. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ a $*$-representation. Assume $\pi$ is nonzero irreducible and that every nonzero irreducible representation of $A$ of $A$ is unitarily equivalent to it. Let $\widehat\pi(\lambda,a)=\lambda I_H+\pi(a)$ be its unital extension to $\widetilde A=\mathbb C\oplus A$. Write $\iota(a)=(0,a)$ and $\chi_\infty(\lambda,a)=\lambda$. Let $D\subseteq\widetilde A$ be a norm-closed unital $*$-subalgebra and $\chi$ a character of $D$ distinct from $\chi_\infty|_D$. Then there is $\eta\in H$ such that $$\|\eta\|=1,\qquad \widehat\pi(d)\eta=\chi(d)\eta\quad(d\in D).$$
content.assumptions: No separability of $H$ is assumed, and $D$ is not assumed commutative. The existence of the specified character of $D$ is part of the input.
content.conclusion: One unit vector is a joint eigenvector for every $d\in D$, with eigenvalues given by the very same prescribed character $\chi$.
content.proof_summary: Extend the character to a pure state; prove that its GNS restriction is nonzero; use the singleton comparison and the zero GNS norm of a centered element.
proof_steps: Apply [Pure-state extension of the prescribed character](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/State/Extension.lean#L231-L258) to this closed unital $*$-subalgebra $D$ of the nonzero unital $\widetilde A$ and its character $\chi$. Obtain a pure state $\varphi$ on $\widetilde A$ with $\varphi|_D=\chi$. Let $(H_\varphi,\rho_U,\xi)$ be its GNS representation, where $\|\xi\|=1$, and restrict it by $\rho(a)=\rho_U(\iota(a))$.

If $\rho(a)=0$ for every $a\in A$, the GNS identity would give $\varphi(\iota(a))=\langle\xi,\rho(a)\xi\rangle=0$. Complex linearity and normalization would then give $$\varphi(\lambda,a)=\lambda=\chi_\infty(\lambda,a).$$ Restricting to $D$ contradicts $\chi\ne\chi_\infty|_D$. Thus $\rho$ is nonzero. Purity gives irreducibility of $\rho_U$ by [Pure-state GNS irreducibility](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/State/Irreducible.lean#L127-L144). Reducing subspaces for $\rho$ also reduce $\lambda I+\rho(a)$, so $\rho$ is irreducible.

Apply the singleton condition to this nonzero irreducible $\rho$ to obtain a unitary equivalence. Extending it to the unitizations supplies a unitary $V:H\to H_\varphi$ with $$V\widehat\pi(z)=\rho_U(z)V\qquad(z\in\widetilde A).$$ We use this chosen $V$ for the rest of the argument. It is unnecessary to identify it with a separately chosen earlier intertwiner.

For $d\in D$, put $q=d-\chi(d)1\in D$. Multiplicativity and preservation of adjoints give $\chi(q)=0$ and $\chi(q^*q)=0$. Since the extension agrees with $\chi$ on $D$, the GNS identity yields $$\|\rho_U(q)\xi\|^2=\varphi(q^*q)=\chi(q^*q)=0.$$ Therefore $\rho_U(d)\xi=\chi(d)\xi$.

Set $\eta=V^{-1}\xi$. Unitarity gives $\|\eta\|=\|\xi\|=1$. Substituting this same vector into the intertwining equation gives $$V\widehat\pi(d)\eta=\rho_U(d)\xi=\chi(d)\xi=V(\chi(d)\eta).$$ Cancel the injective $V$ to obtain the stated joint eigenvector equations.
